title: Most neurons are already interpretable ("neural networks are already clean")
description: A claim that most neurons have coherent, identifiable roles.
bottom_line: The estimate that about 90% of Qwen3-32B neurons' positive or negative sides have one main job comes from one preliminary audit with no independent check. Similar shares across other models remain unconfirmed. Independent studies show that architecture, training and interpretation tools affect interpretability, but layer width also matters, and explanations fitting selected examples can mispredict activations. Graphs built from models' own neurons can explain behaviour in 2B–9B models, with substantial task-dependent limits. Whether most neurons have coherent roles remains open, especially in larger models, where outside evidence is sparse.

claims.heading: Qwen3-32B neuron sides (positive/negative): ~90% one main job, ~7% two, ~2–4% not yet understood
claims.summary: Only the original essay reports these shares, from a preliminary audit that gives no sample size, method or error bar. No independent study has tested this split in Qwen3-32B, so the figures remain the author's estimates.

claims.heading: Dense and mixture-of-experts models have similar one-job neuron shares, up to trillions of parameters
claims.summary: So far only the original essay reports similar shares across dense and mixture-of-experts models, and it has no full audit above 100B parameters. Independent studies match only parts of the claim, such as a small uninterpretable share in two dense 7B models, while a Qwen-2.5-32B test found one consistent explanation for only 67.1% of neurons.

claims.heading: Classic 'polysemantic' neurons, like InceptionV1's cat-and-car neuron, detect one feature their categories share
claims.summary: Only the original essay reports this reading, from its author's own inspection of one neuron and one circuit, with no blind check (one where the rater does not know the expected answer). No independent study supports or challenges it; one study of a different InceptionV1 neuron found mixed results, depending on the strength of an L1 sparsity penalty, that point toward superposition (features sharing neurons).

claims.heading: Messy neurons come from architecture, regularization and weak tools, not capacity
claims.summary: Independent groups show that architecture, regularization and interpretation tools change how interpretable units are in vision CNNs, GANs, toy models and small language models, though some newer designs lower interpretability rather than raise it. Several studies also find that layer width matters, against the 'not capacity' part, and no other study measures the essay's estimated rise in interpretable neurons from about 5% to about 99%.

claims.heading: Attribution graphs on a large model's own neurons explain behaviour without a stand-in model
claims.summary: Two independent groups find attribution graphs built from neurons in 2B–9B Gemma and Llama models faithful and competitive with stand-in graphs built on SAEs or transcoders, though some transcoders still score higher. The limits depend on task and model: Gemma-2-2B subject–verb agreement circuits need about 50,000 neurons to recover half the task performance, Llama-3.1 neuron circuits on ARC score close to random, and above 9B there are only the original's single-prompt demonstrations.

claims.heading: Explanations fitting a neuron's activating examples can mispredict its firing, so inspection overstates understanding
claims.summary: Independent groups find such mispredictions in GPT-2, Gemma 2, Llama 3.1 and several vision models, and how large the failure is depends on layer and explanation method. Only the original essay tests whether 'one main job' judgments made by inspection overstate what is explained, and it found failures for a minority of the Qwen3-32B neurons it tested.

claims.heading: Only a minority of neuron explanations predict activations well, even from stronger explainers
claims.summary: Several independent groups report low average simulation scores (how well an explanation predicts activations) for neuron explanations on GPT-2 XL, small GPT-2 and CRATE (white-box transformer) models, and Gemma 2. Outside the original, only an informal 50-neuron post reproduces the finding that just a minority of neurons are well explained, and the evidence that stronger explainers still leave most neurons poorly scored is indirect.

related_findings.title: Dictionary feature quality varies with design, layer and domain
related_findings.summary: How interpretable, pure and stable SAE and other dictionary features (not neurons) are depends on domain, layer and design choices such as L0, width, architecture and supervision. Automated scores range from below permutation controls to high, and dictionaries recover features imperfectly and vary by seed.

examples.headline: In toy models, SAE latents mix correlated features unless L0 is set correctly.
On matched GPT-2 layer 7, absorption varies about 12-fold across SAE architectures.
Supervised TaxoSAE puts each higher-level taxonomy concept on about one latent; unsupervised SAEs spread it widely.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Small selected neuron sets control specific behaviours
related_findings.summary: Small, statistically selected neuron sets, often under 1% of neurons, causally control or predict behaviours such as arithmetic, programming language, refusal, bias and knowledge recall, well beyond random-neuron controls. The pattern holds in LLMs, vision-language, audio-language and vision models, and several studies read these sets as population-level readouts rather than one neuron per job.

examples.headline: Ablating 320 arithmetic neurons cuts Llama3-8B addition accuracy to 0.3%; random ablation does not.
Ablating language-specific neurons, under 0.7% of all, sharply cuts pass@3 in that programming language.
Clamping top 2,500 safety neurons (5,000 for Qwen2.5-32B) cuts average attack success to at most 2.0%.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Dictionary features and other directions often beat native neurons
related_findings.summary: Rated by the same tools or raters, sparse dictionary features and other non-neuron directions are more often interpretable, concept-selective or steerable than native neurons. This holds in language, vision, ECG and other scientific models, though much of the language-model evidence comes from small transformers.

examples.headline: SAE features beat top-k neurons on interpretability scores (fuzzing, detection) in Gemma 2 and Llama 3.1.
Crowdworkers gave Pythia-70M SAE features mean ratings of 53–82, neurons 30–36, out of 100.
In vision-language-action models, 70–90% of SAE features were labelled interpretable, versus 30% of FFN neurons.

sources.source_id: TITLE:Language models can explain neurons in language models

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Top-example explanations only partly predict full activation range
related_findings.summary: Explanations built from top-activating examples, for SAE features, vision units and some neurons, only partly predict activation on held-out, lower-range, near-neighbour, out-of-domain or inhibitory inputs. Active hypothesis testing improves them.

examples.headline: Least-activating patches suppress most final-layer units in three vision models; top-patch explanations miss this.
GPT-2 SAE explanations from top examples alone score worse than ones sampled across activations.
Iterative hypothesis testing lifts SAE-feature simulation correlations from 0.52–0.70 to 0.65–0.83.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Function is distributed across populations, not single units
related_findings.summary: Neurons or features picked by correlation, selectivity or a well-scoring explanation are often causally insufficient, and aligned subspaces or populations beat single neurons. Neuron selections are only partly specific to the concept and dataset.

examples.headline: Toxic-labelled neurons explain only 0.41%–23.9% of DPO's toxicity reduction.
The neuron most correlated with evaluation awareness fails an ablation-based causal check at 3B and 8B.
Toy Transformer: neuron patching reaches 0.59–0.73 interchange-intervention accuracy; learned rotated bases (DAS) reach at least 0.95.

sources.source_id: TITLE:Language models can explain neurons in language models

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Dictionary features as causal control units
related_findings.summary: Selected SAE features and other dictionary units (not neurons) can act as concept-selective causal controls in language, diffusion, vision, weather, ECG, protocol and music models. The effects depend on the baseline, model and judge, can be undone by fine-tuning, and can produce out-of-distribution artifacts.

examples.headline: Removing concept-aligned SAE features cuts Qwen3-0.6B accuracy to 4.2%, against 46.8% for random.
SAE ablation beats all-layer dense steering in Gemma-2-9B but loses to same-layer baselines.
Fine-tuning on deceptive data undoes DistilGPT-2 deception-feature ablation within a few epochs.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Architecture and training choices change neuron monosemanticity
related_findings.summary: Constraints such as activation or weight sparsity, TopK-style competition, decorrelation, concept supervision and weight decay raise measured unit monosemanticity in small networks without removing polysemantic units. GLU gating and late ViT layers lower it.

examples.headline: In a legible-by-construction transformer, added constraints lift on/off, input-dependent units from 2% to 78%.
On modular addition, GLU neurons are less Fourier-concentrated than plain FFN neurons (0.17 vs 0.34).
43% of ViT-B block-11 neurons look polysemantic by a dip test; ResNet-50 stays unimodal.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Many language-model neurons carry several behaviours
related_findings.summary: In small-to-mid language models, many MLP neurons, especially in early layers, show several behaviours, fire on unrelated content or resist labelling. How large the polysemantic share is depends strongly on the measure.

examples.headline: In Gemma, Qwen and Llama models, each frequently active neuron's explanations form 2.2–5.5 clusters on average.
Strongly connected neurons that are polysemantic make up under 5% of each Pythia-70M and GPT-2-Small layer.
Many early-layer Pythia neurons fire on many unrelated n-grams, suggesting heavier superposition.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Interpretable-unit shares outside language models vary widely
related_findings.summary: Outside language models, estimated shares of interpretable units vary widely by model, layer and method. They range from most units in some ResNet late layers, and about two thirds in others, to under 1% in a tabular foundation model tested against predefined concepts.

examples.headline: Manual inspection judged 69% of sampled ResNet-18 final-layer units meaningful, 31% polysemantic.
Only a few hundred of 2048 ResNet-50 penultimate neurons look polysemantic by CLIP clustering.
Under 1% of TabPFN neurons are significantly salient and selective for any predefined ICD concept.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Training regime and data shift unit-level concept alignment
related_findings.summary: Training regime, data, objective and architecture change how many vision and audio units align with labelled concepts and which concept types they detect. The direction of the change depends on the model.

examples.headline: Vanilla distillation gives ResNet-18 312 concept detectors, against 275 trained from scratch.
A concept-diversity regularizer raised interpretable neurons in ResNet-18 but lowered them in ResNet-50.
Magnitude pruning ResNet-50 to about 16.8% of weights leaves the number of interpretable units unchanged.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Interpretability measures depend on tool, metric and explainer
related_findings.summary: How many units count as interpretable, and which labels they get, depends strongly on the labelling tool, metric, threshold, concept vocabulary, probing data and explainer model. Newer tools label more vision units, so coverage alone is not evidence of clean units.

examples.headline: Different labelling tools label anywhere from 191 to all 512 final-layer CNN filters.
GPT-4V-based discovery labelled 99 of 100 ResNet50 final-layer units; FALCON labelled 11.
Qwen2.5-3B SAE explanations clearing 0.2 correlation range from 43.11% to 80.46% by explainer.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Interpretability scores can be inflated, manipulated or unreliable
related_findings.summary: Simulation and detection scores can reward generic explanations or exploit cues in how test items are built and random negatives, and embedding-based scores track encoder anisotropy. Human forced-choice tests score above chance even with uninformative references, and probing data, visualizations and top-k images can be altered without changing model behaviour.

examples.headline: Simple rules based on item structure beat LLM scorers on Neuronpedia's stored GPT-2 small fuzzing tests.
Corrupting probing data changed Network Dissection concepts for up to ~96–100% of higher-layer units.
38% of sampled Delphi explanations failed review; authors say LLM scorers favour simple explanations.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Few units recur across seeds, architectures or dictionary fits
related_findings.summary: Few individual neurons recur across seeds or architectures, and those that recur tend to be more interpretable. SAE features align across architectures better than raw neurons, but individual dictionary features often fail to reproduce across fits, sizes or paraphrases, while organisation-level patterns recur.

examples.headline: Only about 1–5% of neurons are universal across seeds; these usually have clear interpretations.
Best-matched Pythia and Mamba SAE features correlate 0.74 on average; raw neuron activations only 0.30.
Across SAEs sharing one initialization, only 11.3–13.9% of latents keep the same top-activating token position.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Toy models: where polysemanticity comes from
related_findings.summary: In toy models, polysemanticity arises from feature sparsity and capacity pressure, but also without capacity pressure, from initialization, training dynamics, correlated features or combinatorial codes. Routing sparsity and splitting neurons reduce it.

examples.headline: Toy ReLU autoencoders develop polysemantic neurons even with at least as many neurons as features.
Small Boolean MLPs show polysemantic neurons even with more neurons than features.
Toy MoEs show less superposition as experts increase; dense models keep lower reconstruction loss.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Own-unit circuits versus replacement-model attribution graphs
related_findings.summary: Circuits built from a model's own units or weights can reproduce task behaviour, and neuron-level causal edges in tiny MLPs agree with standard circuit-discovery methods. Transcoder replacement graphs need error nodes to stay faithful, and high attribution does not imply causal sufficiency.

examples.headline: A Llama-2-7B-chat transcoder graph matches outputs only when error nodes are kept.
Holding Gemma-2-2B's top-attributed units fixed preserves outputs only 31–50% of the time; WASD-chosen sets, ~92%.
Pruned GPT-2 small subnetworks keep 93.1–100% task accuracy, but per-relation PARAREL fact-recall test accuracy is 57.7–95.6%.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Unit concepts and interpretability vary with layer depth
related_findings.summary: The kind of concept a unit matches, and how well its explanation holds, change systematically with layer depth. No single direction holds across models and methods.

examples.headline: GAN generator: object and part units concentrate in layers 4–7, materials and shapes later.
In VGG-19, mammal concept-classifier F1 rises from 0.04 to about 0.8 with depth.
In robot policy π0.5, the share of motion-verb neurons rises from 25.8% to 40.3% with depth.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Native neurons sometimes match or beat dictionary features
related_findings.summary: On some 1-D probing and causal-localization tests, native neurons match or beat SAE and transcoder features, and much dictionary activity, especially in late layers, duplicates single MLP neurons. Neurons still miss some rare fine-grained concepts such as bigrams, and SAE reconstruction error can cost model knowledge.

examples.headline: The best single MLP neuron beats single SAE features on 1-D probes of 113 concepts.
Most SAEs fall below the GPT-2 small neuron basis on country disentanglement.
Transcoder features aligned to single neurons supply 38.0–82.8% of all feature activations.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Apparent polysemanticity often reflects one coherent feature
related_findings.summary: Many neurons that look polysemantic respond to one coherent shared feature, such as word form, pose variants, shifted motifs, related concepts or slices of one manifold. Vision neurons that mix related concepts share more upstream circuitry than those mixing unrelated ones, so polysemanticity estimates can overstate how much unrelated concepts are mixed.

examples.headline: Across nine transformers, one word's different senses share more MLP neurons than synonyms do.
ResNet-50 channel 1721 fires on dog faces, with weakly distinct pose or viewpoint subclusters.
Pythia expert neurons are polysemantic along interpretable lines: 'cat' overlaps 'dog', not 'car'.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Whole MoE experts as interpretable units
related_findings.summary: Whole MoE experts can get short labels that predict held-out routing or activation moderately to well, more so under sparser routing. But the features routing to one expert span many semantic clusters, and expert labels are broader than those of their neurons.

examples.headline: In Qwen3-30B-A3B, routing each token to more experts makes expert-level explanations predict less accurately.
LLM labels for whole MoE experts mostly score F1 above 0.8 on held-out detection.
Each MoE expert's best-predicting SAE latents span many semantic clusters: 10.8–11.3 of 20 on average.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Is the neuron basis privileged? It depends
related_findings.summary: CNN unit interpretability drops under random rotation, and activation functions privilege their own basis. But BERT [CLS] and residual-stream bases are no more interpretable than random directions, and unit-level decompositions miss task or content/style separations that linear subspaces recover.

examples.headline: Randomly rotating AlexNet conv5's basis cuts unique concept detectors by 80%, with unchanged discriminative power.
Small autoencoders with tanh-like activations align latents with axes the activation favors, not random ones.
In tanh RNNs, linear decompositions find task-specific components that unit-level decompositions miss.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Most attention heads do several jobs
related_findings.summary: Most attention heads appear to do several jobs, some of them related, while a minority are monosemantic. Some head roles concentrate in a single direction.

examples.headline: Only 14 of 144 GPT-2 Small attention heads look plausibly monosemantic.
Pythia-160M Lorsa heads (sparse attention decompositions) get LLM-simulation interpretability scores roughly matching attention-output SAE features.
In late-layer OpenCLIP-L heads, the first principal component alone sometimes matches the whole head's text description.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Rule-like neurons in small game- and task-trained models
related_findings.summary: In small game- or task-trained models such as OthelloGPT, a substantial share of neurons in some layers act as rule-like detectors. Their causal roles are pattern-specific but incomplete.

examples.headline: Depth-4 decision trees on board features predict 913 of 2,048 layer-5 OthelloGPT neurons well.
610 OthelloGPT neurons predict move-enabling board patterns with F1 above 0.99.
Keeping only OthelloGPT neurons for active tile-flipping rules mostly did no better than ablating all neurons.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: No single scale or fine-tuning trend in monosemanticity
related_findings.summary: Proxy measures of neuron monosemanticity show no single trend with scale or fine-tuning: some fall with scale, some show no ordering by model size, and neurons matched across models grow more selective. DPO moves the measures up in some layers and down in others, and fine-tuning repurposes many pretrained vision neurons.

examples.headline: Across Pythia 70M–6.9B, neuron monosemanticity scores fall with model scale.
A weight-based monosemanticity proxy shows no ordering by size; DPO raises early-layer values, lowers late-layer ones.
Rosetta neurons, matched across models, grow sublinearly in number with scale and become more selective.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Concepts spread over groups of SAE latents
related_findings.summary: Part-of-speech categories, physical-event attributes and legal factors are carried by groups of SAE latents rather than one latent per concept, and some latents serve two related categories. These are SAE features, not neurons.

examples.headline: In a LLaMA-3-8B SAE, part-of-speech tags map to compact latent groups that partly overlap.
In a GraphCast SAE, position and pressure relations use modest feature sets; intensity uses many features.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

reading_list.why: The source essay: roughly 90% of Qwen3-32B neuron poles have one main job, per an unchecked preliminary audit.

reading_list.source_id: TITLE:Language models can explain neurons in language models
reading_list.why: The baseline automated-explanation study: GPT-4 explained all 307,200 GPT-2 XL neurons; only 1.7% scored above 0.7.
Closest outside check of the essay's share: in Qwen-2.5-32B-Instruct, an LLM judge rated 32.9% of sampled neurons polysemantic (multi-meaning).

known_gaps.summary: The headline share has no independent check, outside evidence thins out above 10B and mostly concerns smaller models or other units, and several lines of evidence still conflict.
items: The essay's headline share, roughly 90% of Qwen3-32B neuron sides (positive or negative) with one main job, rests only on its own preliminary audit, which gives no sample size, judge or threshold. No outside audit of neuron sides in Qwen3-32B or a similar model has been found so far, and some studies that may report such shares have not yet been checked.

No neuron-level study above 100B parameters tests any of the claims; the only result at that scale, shown only in figures, is how well explanations of whole experts predict activity in the mixture-of-experts Qwen3-235B-A22B, and the essay's claim that its picture holds up to trillion-parameter models rests on one Kimi K3 graph with no ablation. Outside the essay, circuit evidence stops at about 9B, and no test of how well neuron or feature explanations predict activations covers 10–100B.

No study compares neuron job shares between base and post-trained versions of a model, or across sizes within one family. Proxy measures disagree: one study of Pythia 70M–6.9B finds a proxy for monosemanticity (neurons with a single meaning) falling with scale, while another finds no ordering by size and a shift after preference tuning (DPO) that goes opposite ways in early and late layers.

Most outside evidence concerns GPT-2 XL, small language models, SAE features, vision units or narrow circuit tasks, not neurons of a modern large model. Architecture evidence comes mostly from vision CNNs, GANs, toy and purpose-built models, and how GLU gating affects neurons, compared with a plain feed-forward layer, has been tested only in a toy model and in small chess-playing transformers.

Some studies find dictionary features more interpretable than neurons, while others find native neurons match or beat them. Likewise, small selected neuron sets control behaviours in some studies while others find function spread across populations, and neither tension is resolved.

The claim that apparently polysemantic neurons hide one coherent feature rests on the essay alone. The only outside test looks at a different InceptionV1 neuron and points to superposition (features sharing neurons), and work on language-model neurons that detect word forms and on ResNet-50 channels has not yet been compared with it.

It has not been checked whether the studies supporting the claims are independent of the original authors. Some studies shown here as separate report the same experiments, so the independent evidence may be thinner than it looks.
